Playbook.name: Windows — New Interactive RDP Logon to a Host - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A first-seen (account -> host) interactive RDP logon (4624 LogonType 10) fired via new_terms. Triage question: is this a user/admin RDPing somewhere they normally do not, which could be lateral movement, or simply a new-but-legitimate access relationship?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: RDP is a primary lateral-movement and hands-on-keyboard channel; a new RDP relationship to a sensitive host can be an attacker pivoting.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: New RDP relationship
Signal.Details: 4624 LogonType 10, first observed (user,host) pair in the history window.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Admins RDP to new servers routinely; concern rises when the destination is sensitive (DC, Tier-0, PCI/SWIFT segment) or the source is unusual for the user.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether this new RDP relationship is routine admin/user access or an anomalous pivot to a sensitive host.

Step.name: Characterise the RDP session and source
Step.Purpose: Establish the source and whether the same account is opening RDP to several hosts (fan-out = movement).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.LogonType == "10" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS sessions = COUNT(*), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), host_list = VALUES(host.name) BY src | SORT sessions DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: One user RDPing to many hosts from one source in a short window = fan-out/lateral movement. A single new destination from the user's normal workstation = likely benign new access.

Step.name: Was the RDP preceded by failed logons (brute) to this host
Step.Purpose: RDP success preceded by failures to the same host/account suggests guessed access rather than authorised use.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code == "4625" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS fails = COUNT(*), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), srcs = VALUES(source.ip) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A burst of 4625 to this host just before the successful RDP, especially for the same account/source, upgrades suspicion toward brute-forced RDP.

Step.name: Post-logon privileged actions on the destination
Step.Purpose: Hands-on-keyboard follow-on (special privileges, new services) indicates active operation, not a benign check-in.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("4672","4688","7045","4720","4728") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Account creation, service install or privilege use right after the RDP points to hands-on attacker activity.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows fan-out (one account RDPing to many hosts) or INV-02 shows preceding brute-force to the destination.
Node.Result: True Positive (Lateral Movement via RDP - escalate)

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows privileged follow-on (new service/account/privileges) on a sensitive destination.
Single new destination from the user's normal workstation, destination not sensitive, no follow-on.
New RDP to a sensitive host (DC/Tier-0/PCI/SWIFT) by an admin without a change record.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-RDP-SESSION, INV-02-RDP-PRECEDING, INV-03-RDP-ACTIONS to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate new administrative or user RDP relationship.

Indicators.Item: No brute-force precursor, no privileged follow-on.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm with the user/owner if needed; close as benign_activity; new_terms will learn the pair.

TruePositive.Definition: An attacker using RDP to pivot between hosts.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate destination and source; reset the account; revoke sessions.
Hunt the account's other RDP targets; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A monitoring/jump product opening RDP in a new pattern after a config change.

Indicators.Item: A known jump-host/PAM system as source.
New destination due to onboarding, not attack.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the PAM/jump change; document so new_terms learns it.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If fan-out/brute precursor: isolate hosts, reset account.
Confirm the source with the user for sensitive destinations.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Hunt lateral spread from the source; review destination for persistence.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restrict RDP to jump hosts/PAM; enforce MFA on RDP; tier admin access.

QualityChecks.Check: new_terms keys on (user,host) - legitimate new admin access fires once then is learned.
Destination sensitivity should raise severity - maintain a Tier-0/PCI/SWIFT host list for triage.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Benign new access confirmed; destination not sensitive.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Lateral movement scoped, hosts isolated, account reset, IR recorded.
